summary_oneline: PBAC example: add_policy() URI grants never reach the evaluator (428 on /dashboard/), plus log noise, a 6-byte JWT key and an unmigrated v1 vault secret.

localization.role: decides URI access through the PolicyEvaluator only; raises PreconditionFailed (428) when no policy matched
public API that appends a classic Policy to self._policies only; never adapts it into the evaluator
startup storage load; returns early at line 115 when the evaluator already holds policies
the only path that adapts policies (PolicyAdapter.adapt_batch) and loads them into the evaluator
converts a classic Policy dict into a ResourcePolicy (subjects, tenant (1,1) default)
builds the HTTP 428 error returned to the browser
pre-loads the evaluator (load_from_directory at 560, load_policies at 563) then registers URI policies via pdp.add_policy (586)
the only ALLOW policy for urn:uri:/dashboard/ (no subject constraint)
logs 'Access to X is not Authenticated.' at WARNING (line 43) for every unauthenticated, non-excluded request, then passes it through; duplicate except at 47-56
per-app fnmatch exclude list API used by the example
AUTH_SECRET_KEY taken verbatim, no minimum length; random 32-byte fallback only when unset
HS256 jwt.encode/decode with SECRET_KEY — triggers PyJWT InsecureKeyLengthWarning
per-row open; logs 'failed integrity check', audits integrity_fail, skips the row (dependency code)
raised for any blob that is not a v2 (0xA2) envelope (dependency code)
the April 2026 migration that made authorize() evaluator-only while promising an unchanged PDP public interface; add_policy not covered

constraints.statement: The 'skip storage load when the evaluator is pre-populated' guard is intentional and pinned by tests/test_yaml_storage_double_load.py::TestPDPDoubleLoadPrevention
constraints.implication: the fix must not reintroduce double-loading of YAML/DB policies; route add_policy() into the evaluator instead of removing the guard

constraints.statement: PDP.authorize consults only the evaluator; self._policies is kept only 'for backward compatibility'
constraints.implication: any policy that must affect authorization has to be adapted and loaded into the evaluator

constraints.statement: Default effect is deny (ABAC_DEFAULT_EFFECT fallback 'deny'; every default YAML pack declares defaults.effect: deny); the Rust engine fails closed on errors
constraints.implication: the fix must keep fail-closed semantics — no allow-by-default shortcut

constraints.statement: No test covers the 428 no-match path or PDP.add_policy
constraints.implication: the fix needs regression tests for add_policy -> evaluator and for the 428 response

constraints.statement: abac_middleware's warning branch is a pass-through (request still served); tests/test_probes.py references a separate probe tracker for repeated unauthenticated probes
constraints.implication: demoting/filtering the log must not change authorization behaviour or the probe tracker

constraints.statement: SECRET_KEY also signs IdP authorization codes/JWTs and CSRF tokens; PARTNER_KEY (16 bytes) is the fallback for AUTH_TOKEN_SECRET
constraints.implication: rotating the key invalidates in-flight tokens; a startup check must cover both keys and choose warn vs fail deliberately

constraints.statement: Vault envelope/SessionVault code lives in the navigator-session dependency; loading is fail-closed per row by design (FEAT-099)
constraints.implication: the vault error is an operational migration step (navigator-vault migrate), not a navigator-auth code change

constraints.statement: The classic->Rust migration spec promised an unchanged PDP public interface
constraints.implication: restoring add_policy's effect is a bug fix to honour that contract, not a new API

hypotheses.statement: The example's URI grants (public_dashboard etc.) are registered with PDP.add_policy, which never loads them into the PolicyEvaluator; because the example pre-populates the evaluator, PDP._load_policies also skips storage, and PDP.authorize — which asks only the evaluator — finds no policy for /dashboard/ and raises the 428.
hypotheses.reasoning: Every link is read directly and probe-verified at HEAD c25272a. F014 dates the gap to the April 2026 classic->Rust migration, which explains why no recent commit shows it; still not reproduced at runtime.
hypotheses.next_probe: After pdp.setup(app) at examples/policy_server.py:589, print [p.name for p in pdp._evaluator._index.all()] and confirm public_dashboard is absent; then GET /dashboard/ logged in and expect 428.

hypotheses.statement: Before the pre-load guard landed in PDP._load_policies, startup also loaded DB/YAML storage policies into the evaluator, so a /dashboard/ grant stored in the example database used to match.
hypotheses.reasoning: Would explain 'was working before', but the guard's landing date and the example DB contents were not researched (git budget exhausted).

hypotheses.statement: The 2026-10-13 session-user rehydration change (normalize_memberships on every request, decode errors return no user) altered the subject so subject-scoped policies stop matching.
hypotheses.reasoning: A 428 means no policy matched the resource at all, and public_dashboard has no subject constraint, so H1 explains the symptom without this change.
hypotheses.next_probe: Search the server log for 'NAV: Unable to decode User session' (auth.py:755).

unknowns.question: Where should the 428 fix go: make PDP.add_policy load classic policies into the evaluator (library), rewrite the example's URI policies as evaluator-native policies (example only), or both?
unknowns.user_answer: Library + example: make PDP.add_policy() load classic policies into the evaluator (keep the startup-load guard), add regression tests, and clean up the example.

unknowns.question: How should the 'Access to X is not Authenticated' noise be handled: demote it to DEBUG, add default exclusions for browser probe paths (/favicon.ico, /.well-known/*), or both?
unknowns.user_answer: Both: demote the message to DEBUG, add default exclusions for /favicon.ico and /.well-known/*, and remove the duplicate dead except clause.

unknowns.question: For HMAC keys shorter than 32 bytes (AUTH_SECRET_KEY, AUTH_TOKEN_SECRET/PARTNER_KEY): warn at startup, refuse to start, or only rotate the env values?
unknowns.user_answer: Warn + rotate env: log a startup warning when AUTH_SECRET_KEY or AUTH_TOKEN_SECRET/PARTNER_KEY is under 32 bytes, and set new 32+ byte env values.

unknowns.question: When did /dashboard/ last work in the example (roughly)?
